decls.name: TauCeti.algebraMap_int_mem_iff_dvd_of_liesOver
decls.doc:
An ideal of a `ℤ`-algebra lying over the integer ideal `(a)` meets `ℤ` exactly in the
multiples of `a`: `algebraMap ℤ S m ∈ Q ↔ a ∣ m`.

decls.name: TauCeti.IsIndecomposableModule
decls.doc:
A module is **indecomposable** when it is nonzero and is not the internal direct sum of two
nonzero submodules.
decls.statement: def IsIndecomposableModule : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.isIndecomposableModule_iff_nontrivial_and_forall_isCompl
decls.doc:
`IsIndecomposableModule` restated as the conjunction defining it, so that clients can
establish and consume it without unfolding the definition.
decls.statement:
theorem isIndecomposableModule_iff_nontrivial_and_forall_isCompl :
    IsIndecomposableModule A M ↔
      Nontrivial M ∧ ∀ N P : Submodule A M, IsCompl N P → N = ⊥ ∨ P = ⊥

decls.name: TauCeti.isIndecomposableModule_of_forall_isCompl
decls.doc:
A nontrivial module along none of whose decompositions `M = N ⊕ P` both summands are nonzero is
indecomposable.
decls.statement:
theorem isIndecomposableModule_of_forall_isCompl [Nontrivial M]
    (h : ∀ N P : Submodule A M, IsCompl N P → N = ⊥ ∨ P = ⊥) : IsIndecomposableModule A M

decls.name: TauCeti.IsIndecomposableModule.nontrivial
decls.statement: theorem IsIndecomposableModule.nontrivial (h : IsIndecomposableModule A M) : Nontrivial M

decls.name: TauCeti.IsIndecomposableModule.eq_bot_or_eq_bot
decls.statement:
theorem IsIndecomposableModule.eq_bot_or_eq_bot (h : IsIndecomposableModule A M)
    {N P : Submodule A M} (hNP : IsCompl N P) : N = ⊥ ∨ P = ⊥

decls.name: TauCeti.IsIndecomposableModule.of_linearEquiv
decls.doc:
Indecomposability transfers along a linear equivalence: the induced order isomorphism of
submodules carries a decomposition of the target back to one of the source.
decls.statement:
theorem IsIndecomposableModule.of_linearEquiv {N : Type w} [AddCommMonoid N] [Module A N]
    (h : IsIndecomposableModule A M) (e : M ≃ₗ[A] N) : IsIndecomposableModule A N

decls.name: TauCeti.IsIndecomposableModule.eq_zero_or_eq_one_of_isIdempotentElem
decls.doc:
The idempotent endomorphisms of an indecomposable module are `0` and `1`: an idempotent splits
the module as the direct sum of its range and its kernel, and one of the two must vanish.
decls.statement:
theorem IsIndecomposableModule.eq_zero_or_eq_one_of_isIdempotentElem
    (h : IsIndecomposableModule A M) {f : Module.End A M} (hf : IsIdempotentElem f) :
    f = 0 ∨ f = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.isIndecomposableModule_of_forall_isIdempotentElem
decls.doc:
A nonzero module whose only idempotent endomorphisms are `0` and `1` is indecomposable: a
decomposition `M = N ⊕ P` is witnessed by the projection onto `N` along `P`.
decls.statement:
theorem isIndecomposableModule_of_forall_isIdempotentElem [Nontrivial M]
    (h : ∀ f : Module.End A M, IsIdempotentElem f → f = 0 ∨ f = 1) :
    IsIndecomposableModule A M

decls.name: TauCeti.isIndecomposableModule_iff_nontrivial_and_forall_isIdempotentElem
decls.doc:
Indecomposability of a module is exactly the statement that it is nontrivial and its
endomorphism ring has no idempotents besides `0` and `1`.
decls.statement:
theorem isIndecomposableModule_iff_nontrivial_and_forall_isIdempotentElem :
    IsIndecomposableModule A M ↔
      Nontrivial M ∧ ∀ f : Module.End A M, IsIdempotentElem f → f = 0 ∨ f = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSimpleModule.isIndecomposableModule
decls.doc: A simple module is indecomposable: it has no proper nonzero submodule to decompose along.
decls.statement:
theorem IsSimpleModule.isIndecomposableModule [IsSimpleModule A M] :
    IsIndecomposableModule A M

decls.name: TauCeti.IsIndecomposableModule.isNilpotent_or_bijective
decls.doc:
**Fitting's lemma**: an endomorphism of an indecomposable module that is both Noetherian and
Artinian is either nilpotent or bijective.

For a large enough exponent `m`, Mathlib's Fitting decomposition splits `M` as
`ker (f ^ m) ⊕ range (f ^ m)`. Indecomposability collapses one of the two summands: if the range
vanishes then `f ^ m = 0`, and if the kernel vanishes then `f` is injective while the range, being
everything, forces `f` to be surjective.
decls.title: Fitting's lemma
decls.statement:
theorem IsIndecomposableModule.isNilpotent_or_bijective (h : IsIndecomposableModule A M)
    (f : Module.End A M) : IsNilpotent f ∨ Function.Bijective f

decls.name: TauCeti.IsIndecomposableModule.isNilpotent_or_isUnit
decls.doc:
**Fitting's lemma**, restated: an endomorphism of an indecomposable module that is both
Noetherian and Artinian is either nilpotent or a unit of the endomorphism ring.
decls.title: Fitting's lemma
decls.statement:
theorem IsIndecomposableModule.isNilpotent_or_isUnit (h : IsIndecomposableModule A M)
    (f : Module.End A M) : IsNilpotent f ∨ IsUnit f

decls.name: TauCeti.IsIndecomposableModule.isNilpotent_iff_not_isUnit
decls.doc:
On an indecomposable module that is Noetherian and Artinian, the non-units of the endomorphism
ring are exactly the nilpotent endomorphisms. This identifies the maximal ideal produced by
`TauCeti.isLocalRing_end_of_isIndecomposable`.
decls.statement:
theorem IsIndecomposableModule.isNilpotent_iff_not_isUnit (h : IsIndecomposableModule A M)
    (f : Module.End A M) : IsNilpotent f ↔ ¬ IsUnit f

decls.name: TauCeti.isLocalRing_end_of_isIndecomposable
decls.doc:
The endomorphism ring of an indecomposable module of finite length is **local**.

This is the form of Fitting's lemma that drives the Krull-Schmidt theorem: a non-unit endomorphism
is nilpotent, and `1 - f` is then a unit.
decls.statement:
theorem isLocalRing_end_of_isIndecomposable (hM : IsFiniteLength A M)
    (h : IsIndecomposableModule A M) : IsLocalRing (Module.End A M)

decls.name: TauCeti.isIndecomposableModule_of_isLocalRing_end
decls.doc:
A nonzero module with local endomorphism ring is indecomposable. This is the converse of
`TauCeti.isLocalRing_end_of_isIndecomposable`, and needs no finiteness hypothesis.
decls.statement:
theorem isIndecomposableModule_of_isLocalRing_end [Nontrivial M]
    [IsLocalRing (Module.End A M)] : IsIndecomposableModule A M

decls.name: TauCeti.isIndecomposableModule_iff_nontrivial_and_isLocalRing_end
decls.doc:
For a module of finite length, indecomposability is **equivalent** to being nontrivial and
having a local endomorphism ring.
decls.statement:
theorem isIndecomposableModule_iff_nontrivial_and_isLocalRing_end (hM : IsFiniteLength A M) :
    IsIndecomposableModule A M ↔ Nontrivial M ∧ IsLocalRing (Module.End A M)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsLocalRing.eq_zero_or_eq_one_of_isIdempotentElem
decls.doc:
An idempotent of a local ring is `0` or `1`. Mathlib's
`IsLocalRing.isUnit_or_isUnit_one_sub_self` is stated over a commutative ring, so the splitting of
`1 = a + (1 - a)` is taken here from `IsLocalRing.isUnit_or_isUnit_of_isUnit_add`, which holds over
any semiring.
decls.statement:
theorem IsLocalRing.eq_zero_or_eq_one_of_isIdempotentElem {R : Type*} [Ring R] [IsLocalRing R]
    {a : R} (ha : IsIdempotentElem a) : a = 0 ∨ a = 1

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.isUnit_leadingCoeff_T
decls.doc: The leading coefficient of every Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind over `R` is a unit.
decls.statement: lemma isUnit_leadingCoeff_T (n : ℕ) : IsUnit (T R n).leadingCoeff

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.chebyshevTBasis
decls.doc:
The Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind, indexed by their nonnegative degree, form a
basis of `R[X]`.
decls.statement: def chebyshevTBasis : Module.Basis ℕ R R[X]

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.chebyshevTBasis_apply
decls.doc: The `n`th vector of the Chebyshev basis is `T R n`.
decls.statement: lemma chebyshevTBasis_apply (n : ℕ) : chebyshevTBasis n = T R n

decls.name: Polynomial.derivative_hermite_succ
decls.doc:
**Lowering (derivative) identity for the Hermite polynomials.** Differentiating the
`(n + 1)`-st probabilists' Hermite polynomial lowers the index:
`H'_{n+1} = (n + 1) · Hₙ`.
decls.title: Lowering (derivative) identity for the Hermite polynomials
decls.statement:
theorem _root_.Polynomial.derivative_hermite_succ (n : ℕ) :
    derivative (hermite (n + 1)) = (n + 1) • hermite n

decls.name: Polynomial.derivative_hermite
decls.doc:
The Hermite derivative identity restated at index `n`: `H'ₙ = n · Hₙ₋₁`. For `n = 0` both sides
vanish (`H₀ = 1`).
decls.statement:
theorem _root_.Polynomial.derivative_hermite (n : ℕ) :
    derivative (hermite n) = n • hermite (n - 1)

decls.name: Polynomial.iterate_derivative_hermite
decls.doc:
Iterating the lowering identity: the `k`-th derivative of `Hₙ` is the descending factorial
`n (n-1) ⋯ (n-k+1)` times `H_{n-k}`. For `k > n` the descending factorial is `0` and both sides
vanish.
decls.statement:
theorem _root_.Polynomial.iterate_derivative_hermite (n k : ℕ) :
    derivative^[k] (hermite n) = n.descFactorial k • hermite (n - k)

decls.name: Polynomial.hermite_add_two
decls.doc:
**Three-term recurrence for the Hermite polynomials.** Eliminating the derivative from Mathlib's
defining recursion `hermite_succ` gives the classical relation `H_{n+2} = X·H_{n+1} - (n+1)·Hₙ`,
i.e. `H_{m+1} = X·H_m - m·H_{m-1}`.
decls.title: Three-term recurrence for the Hermite polynomials
decls.statement:
theorem _root_.Polynomial.hermite_add_two (n : ℕ) :
    hermite (n + 2) = X * hermite (n + 1) - (n + 1) • hermite n

decls.name: Polynomial.hermite_aeval_neg
decls.doc:
**Parity of the Hermite polynomials.** `Hₙ(-x) = (-1)ⁿ Hₙ(x)` in any commutative ring: a
coefficient of `hermite n` in degree `k` can be nonzero only when `n + k` is even
(`Polynomial.coeff_hermite_of_odd_add`), so `k` and `n` share parity and `(-x)ᵏ = (-1)ⁿ xᵏ` on every
surviving monomial.
decls.title: Parity of the Hermite polynomials
decls.statement:
theorem _root_.Polynomial.hermite_aeval_neg {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (n : ℕ) (x : R) :
    aeval (-x) (hermite n) = (-1) ^ n * aeval x (hermite n)

decls.name: TauCeti.hasDerivAt_cexp_quadratic
decls.doc: Derivative of the entire function `z ↦ exp (x·z - z²/2)`: its value at `z` times `x - z`.
decls.statement:
theorem hasDerivAt_cexp_quadratic (x z : ℂ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun w : ℂ => Complex.exp (x * w - w ^ 2 / 2))
      (Complex.exp (x * z - z ^ 2 / 2) * (x - z)) z

decls.name: TauCeti.iteratedDeriv_cexp_quadratic
decls.doc:
Closed form for the iterated derivatives of `z ↦ exp (x·z - z²/2)`: the `n`-th derivative at
`z` is `Hₙ(x - z)` times the function value, proved by induction on `n` from the defining recursion
`hermite (n + 1) = X · hermite n - derivative (hermite n)`.
decls.statement:
theorem iteratedDeriv_cexp_quadratic (x : ℂ) (n : ℕ) (z : ℂ) :
    iteratedDeriv n (fun w : ℂ => Complex.exp (x * w - w ^ 2 / 2)) z
      = aeval (x - z) (hermite n) * Complex.exp (x * z - z ^ 2 / 2)

decls.name: TauCeti.hasSum_hermite_generating_function
decls.doc:
**Exponential generating function of the probabilists' Hermite polynomials, summable form.**
For all complex `x` and `t`, the family `Hₙ(x) · tⁿ / n!` is summable with sum
`exp (x · t - t² / 2)`, where `Hₙ = Polynomial.hermite n`.

This is the analytic heart of the identity: it carries the summability that the `tsum` form
`hermite_generating_function` discards, and it holds over all of `ℂ` (the real case is a
specialization by casting).
decls.title: Exponential generating function of the probabilists' Hermite polynomials, summable form
decls.statement:
theorem hasSum_hermite_generating_function (x t : ℂ) :
    HasSum (fun n : ℕ => aeval x (hermite n) * t ^ n / (n.factorial : ℂ))
      (Complex.exp (x * t - t ^ 2 / 2))

decls.name: TauCeti.hermite_generating_function
decls.doc:
**Exponential generating function of the probabilists' Hermite polynomials.** For all real `x`
and `t`,
`∑' n, Hₙ(x) · tⁿ / n! = exp (x · t - t² / 2)`,
where `Hₙ = Polynomial.hermite n`. This is target **A1** of the `OrthogonalL2Bases` roadmap; it is
the real specialization of `hasSum_hermite_generating_function`.
decls.title: Exponential generating function of the probabilists' Hermite polynomials
decls.statement:
theorem hermite_generating_function (x t : ℝ) :
    ∑' n : ℕ, aeval x (hermite n) * t ^ n / (n.factorial : ℝ)
      = Real.exp (x * t - t ^ 2 / 2)

decls.name: TauCeti.hermiteℝ
decls.doc:
`Hₙ` over `ℝ`: Mathlib's `Polynomial.hermite n` lives in `ℤ[X]`, and the analytic consumers
in this library take a real polynomial family.
decls.statement: def hermiteℝ (n : ℕ) : Polynomial ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.eval_hermiteℝ
decls.statement: theorem eval_hermiteℝ (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : (hermiteℝ n).eval x = aeval x (hermite n)

decls.name: TauCeti.degree_hermiteℝ
decls.doc:
The cast to `ℝ[X]` preserves degrees: `Hₙ` has degree exactly `n`.

Marked `@[simp]`, matching Mathlib's own `Polynomial.degree_hermite`.
decls.statement: theorem degree_hermiteℝ (n : ℕ) : (hermiteℝ n).degree = (n : WithBot ℕ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.toMonic
decls.doc:
The monic polynomial `∏_{a ∈ s} (X - a)` of an unordered `n`-tuple `s`, bundled with its
monicity and the fact that its degree is `n`.

The underlying polynomial is Mathlib's `Polynomial.ofMultiset`; the point of the subtype is that
the degree is pinned to `n` rather than to the cardinality of the underlying multiset, which is
what `Polynomial.monicEquivDegreeLT` consumes.
decls.statement: def toMonic (s : Sym R n) : { p : R[X] // p.Monic ∧ p.natDegree = n }

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.coe_toMonic
decls.statement: theorem coe_toMonic (s : Sym R n) : (toMonic s : R[X]) = ofMultiset (s : Multiset R)

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.monic_toMonic
decls.statement: theorem monic_toMonic (s : Sym R n) : (toMonic s : R[X]).Monic

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.natDegree_toMonic
decls.statement: theorem natDegree_toMonic (s : Sym R n) : (toMonic s : R[X]).natDegree = n

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.toMonic_nil
decls.statement: theorem toMonic_nil : (toMonic (Sym.nil : Sym R 0) : R[X]) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.toMonic_cons
decls.doc:
Adjoining a point to a tuple multiplies its monic polynomial by the corresponding linear
factor.
decls.statement:
theorem toMonic_cons (a : R) (s : Sym R n) :
    (toMonic (a ::ₛ s) : R[X]) = (X - C a) * (toMonic s : R[X])

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.toMonic_append
decls.doc:
The monic polynomial of a union of two tuples is the product of their monic polynomials: this
is the multiplicativity that makes `Polynomial.ofMultiset` an additive character.
decls.statement:
theorem toMonic_append (s : Sym R n) (t : Sym R m) :
    (toMonic (s.append t) : R[X]) = (toMonic s : R[X]) * (toMonic t : R[X])

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.toMonic_replicate
decls.doc: The monic polynomial of a constant tuple is a pure power of a linear factor.
decls.statement:
theorem toMonic_replicate (a : R) :
    (toMonic (Sym.replicate n a) : R[X]) = (X - C a) ^ n

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.eval_toMonic
decls.doc:
Evaluating the monic polynomial of a tuple at `x` multiplies together the differences between
`x` and the points of the tuple.
decls.statement:
theorem eval_toMonic (s : Sym R n) (x : R) :
    (toMonic s : R[X]).eval x = ((s : Multiset R).map fun a => x - a).prod

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.coeff_toMonic
decls.doc:
**Vieta's formulas** on the symmetric power: the `k`-th coefficient of the monic polynomial of
an unordered `n`-tuple is the `(n - k)`-th elementary symmetric function of the tuple, up to the
sign `(-1) ^ (n - k)`.
decls.title: Vieta's formulas
decls.statement:
theorem coeff_toMonic (s : Sym R n) {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ n) :
    (toMonic s : R[X]).coeff k = (-1) ^ (n - k) * (s : Multiset R).esymm (n - k)

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.coeff_zero_toMonic
decls.doc: The constant term of the monic polynomial of a tuple is the signed product of its points.
decls.statement:
theorem coeff_zero_toMonic (s : Sym R n) :
    (toMonic s : R[X]).coeff 0 = (-1) ^ n * (s : Multiset R).prod

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.roots_toMonic
decls.doc:
Over an integral domain the points of a tuple are recovered, with multiplicity, as the roots of
its monic polynomial.
decls.statement: theorem roots_toMonic (s : Sym R n) : (toMonic s : R[X]).roots = (s : Multiset R)

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.toMonic_injective
decls.doc:
Over an integral domain a tuple is determined by its monic polynomial: two unordered `n`-tuples
with the same monic polynomial are equal.
decls.statement: theorem toMonic_injective : Function.Injective (toMonic (R := R) (n := n))

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.mem_iff_isRoot
decls.doc: A scalar lies in a tuple exactly when it is a root of the tuple's monic polynomial.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_iff_isRoot {a : R} {s : Sym R n} :
    a ∈ (s : Multiset R) ↔ (toMonic s : R[X]).IsRoot a

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.degreeLTEquiv_toEquiv_apply
decls.doc: `Polynomial.degreeLTEquiv` reads off coefficients.
decls.statement:
theorem degreeLTEquiv_toEquiv_apply (p : degreeLT K n) (i : Fin n) :
    (degreeLTEquiv K n).toEquiv p i = (p : K[X]).coeff (i : ℕ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.coe_monicEquivDegreeLT_apply
decls.doc: `Polynomial.monicEquivDegreeLT` removes the leading term.
decls.statement:
theorem coe_monicEquivDegreeLT_apply (p : { p : K[X] // p.Monic ∧ p.natDegree = n }) :
    ((monicEquivDegreeLT n p : degreeLT K n) : K[X]) = (p : K[X]).eraseLead

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.coe_degreeLTEquiv_toEquiv_symm_apply
decls.doc: The inverse of `Polynomial.degreeLTEquiv` assembles a polynomial from its coefficients.
decls.statement:
theorem coe_degreeLTEquiv_toEquiv_symm_apply (f : Fin n → K) :
    (((degreeLTEquiv K n).toEquiv.symm f : degreeLT K n) : K[X]) =
      ∑ i : Fin n, monomial (i : ℕ) (f i)

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.coe_monicEquivDegreeLT_symm_apply
decls.doc: The inverse of `Polynomial.monicEquivDegreeLT` restores the leading term `X ^ n`.
decls.statement:
theorem coe_monicEquivDegreeLT_symm_apply (p : degreeLT K n) :
    (((monicEquivDegreeLT n).symm p : { p : K[X] // p.Monic ∧ p.natDegree = n }) : K[X]) =
      X ^ n + (p : K[X])

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.monicEquiv
decls.doc:
Over an algebraically closed field, `TauCeti.Sym.toMonic` is a bijection from the `n`-th
symmetric power onto the monic polynomials of degree `n`, inverted by taking roots with
multiplicity.
decls.statement: def monicEquiv : Sym K n ≃ { p : K[X] // p.Monic ∧ p.natDegree = n }

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.monicEquiv_apply
decls.statement: theorem monicEquiv_apply (s : Sym K n) : monicEquiv K n s = toMonic s

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.coe_monicEquiv_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem coe_monicEquiv_symm_apply (p : { p : K[X] // p.Monic ∧ p.natDegree = n }) :
    (((monicEquiv K n).symm p : Sym K n) : Multiset K) = p.1.roots

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.coeffEquiv
decls.doc:
The **elementary symmetric chart** on the `n`-th symmetric power of an algebraically closed
field: an unordered `n`-tuple is determined by, and freely determines, the `n` lower coefficients of
its monic polynomial.

By `TauCeti.Sym.coeffEquiv_apply` the `i`-th coordinate is `(-1) ^ (n - i)` times the `(n - i)`-th
elementary symmetric function of the tuple.
decls.statement: def coeffEquiv : Sym K n ≃ (Fin n → K)

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.coeffEquiv_apply_eq_coeff
decls.doc: The chart reads off the lower coefficients of the monic polynomial of the tuple.
decls.statement:
theorem coeffEquiv_apply_eq_coeff (s : Sym K n) (i : Fin n) :
    coeffEquiv K n s i = (toMonic s : K[X]).coeff i

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.coeffEquiv_apply
decls.doc:
The coordinates of the elementary symmetric chart are the elementary symmetric functions of the
tuple, in decreasing order and with alternating signs.
decls.statement:
theorem coeffEquiv_apply (s : Sym K n) (i : Fin n) :
    coeffEquiv K n s i = (-1) ^ (n - (i : ℕ)) * (s : Multiset K).esymm (n - (i : ℕ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.coeffEquiv_symm_apply
decls.doc:
The inverse chart sends a coefficient tuple to the root multiset of the monic polynomial it
determines.
decls.statement:
theorem coeffEquiv_symm_apply (f : Fin n → K) :
    (((coeffEquiv K n).symm f : Sym K n) : Multiset K) =
      (X ^ n + ∑ i : Fin n, monomial (i : ℕ) (f i)).roots

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.coeffEquiv_one_apply
decls.doc:
In degree one the chart is negation: the single coordinate of a one-point tuple is minus that
point.
decls.statement:
theorem coeffEquiv_one_apply {s : Sym K 1} {a : K} (hs : (s : Multiset K) = {a}) :
    coeffEquiv K 1 s 0 = -a

decls.name: TauCeti.Sym.coeffEquiv_two_apply
decls.doc:
In degree two the chart is `{a, b} ↦ (ab, -(a + b))`: the two lower coefficients of
`(X - a) (X - b) = X ^ 2 - (a + b) X + ab`.
decls.statement:
theorem coeffEquiv_two_apply {s : Sym K 2} {a b : K} (hs : (s : Multiset K) = {a, b}) :
    coeffEquiv K 2 s = ![a * b, -(a + b)]

decls.name: TauCeti.faithfulSMul_of_isSimpleRing
decls.doc:
A nontrivial module over a simple ring is faithful: the elements of `R` killing `M` are the
kernel of a ring homomorphism out of `R`, a two-sided ideal not containing `1`, hence `⊥`.
decls.statement: theorem faithfulSMul_of_isSimpleRing [IsSimpleRing R] [Nontrivial M] : FaithfulSMul R M

decls.name: TauCeti.toModuleEnd_moduleEnd_bijective
decls.doc:
**The double centralizer theorem.** Let `M` be a faithful semisimple `R`-module which is finite
over its endomorphism ring `D = Module.End R M`. Then the natural map `R → Module.End D M` is
bijective: `R` is exactly the ring of `D`-linear endomorphisms of `M`.

This sharpens Mathlib's `Module.Finite.toModuleEnd_moduleEnd_surjective` from surjectivity to
bijectivity; the extra input is faithfulness, which is what makes the map injective.
decls.title: The double centralizer theorem
decls.statement:
theorem toModuleEnd_moduleEnd_bijective [IsSemisimpleModule R M] [FaithfulSMul R M]
    [Module.Finite (Module.End R M) M] :
    Function.Bijective (Module.toModuleEnd (Module.End R M) M (S := R))

decls.name: TauCeti.ringEquivEndEnd
decls.doc:
The double centralizer theorem as a ring isomorphism: a faithful semisimple module finite over
its endomorphism ring `D` identifies `R` with `Module.End D M`.
decls.statement:
def ringEquivEndEnd [IsSemisimpleModule R M] [FaithfulSMul R M]
    [Module.Finite (Module.End R M) M] :
    R ≃+* Module.End (Module.End R M) M

decls.name: TauCeti.ringEquivEndEnd_apply
decls.statement:
theorem ringEquivEndEnd_apply [IsSemisimpleModule R M] [FaithfulSMul R M]
    [Module.Finite (Module.End R M) M] (r : R) (m : M) :
    ringEquivEndEnd R M r m = r • m

decls.name: TauCeti.ringEquivEndEnd_symm_smul
decls.statement:
theorem ringEquivEndEnd_symm_smul [IsSemisimpleModule R M] [FaithfulSMul R M]
    [Module.Finite (Module.End R M) M] (f : Module.End (Module.End R M) M) (m : M) :
    (ringEquivEndEnd R M).symm f • m = f m

decls.name: TauCeti.algEquivEndEnd
decls.doc:
The double centralizer isomorphism as an isomorphism of `K`-algebras, for a commutative base
ring `K` acting on `M` compatibly with `R`.
decls.statement:
def algEquivEndEnd (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] [Algebra K R] [Module K M]
    [IsScalarTower K R M] [IsSemisimpleModule R M] [FaithfulSMul R M]
    [Module.Finite (Module.End R M) M] :
    R ≃ₐ[K] Module.End (Module.End R M) M

decls.name: TauCeti.algEquivEndEnd_apply
decls.statement:
theorem algEquivEndEnd_apply (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] [Algebra K R] [Module K M]
    [IsScalarTower K R M] [IsSemisimpleModule R M] [FaithfulSMul R M]
    [Module.Finite (Module.End R M) M] (r : R) (m : M) :
    algEquivEndEnd R M K r m = r • m

decls.name: TauCeti.algEquivEndEnd_symm_smul
decls.statement:
theorem algEquivEndEnd_symm_smul (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] [Algebra K R] [Module K M]
    [IsScalarTower K R M] [IsSemisimpleModule R M] [FaithfulSMul R M]
    [Module.Finite (Module.End R M) M] (f : Module.End (Module.End R M) M) (m : M) :
    (algEquivEndEnd R M K).symm f • m = f m

decls.name: TauCeti.toModuleEnd_moduleEnd_bijective_of_isSimpleRing
decls.doc:
**The double centralizer theorem for a simple ring.** Over a simple ring every simple module is
automatically faithful, so a simple module finite over its endomorphism ring `D` presents `R` as
`Module.End D M`. This is Wedderburn's theorem for a simple ring, stated without reference to any
base ring.
decls.title: The double centralizer theorem for a simple ring
decls.statement:
theorem toModuleEnd_moduleEnd_bijective_of_isSimpleRing [IsSimpleRing R] [IsSimpleModule R M]
    [Module.Finite (Module.End R M) M] :
    Function.Bijective (Module.toModuleEnd (Module.End R M) M (S := R))

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_smul_eq_of_linearIndependent
decls.doc:
**Jacobson-Chevalley density.** For a simple module `M` finite over `D = Module.End R M`, a
`D`-linearly independent family in `M` can be carried to an arbitrary family of targets by a single
scalar from `R`.

Linear independence is essential: a `D`-linear relation among the `v i` is inherited by the
`r • v i`, so the targets could not be arbitrary.
decls.title: Jacobson-Chevalley density
decls.statement:
theorem exists_smul_eq_of_linearIndependent [IsSimpleModule R M]
    [Module.Finite (Module.End R M) M] {ι : Type*} {v : ι → M}
    (hv : LinearIndependent (Module.End R M) v) (w : ι → M) :
    ∃ r : R, ∀ i, r • v i = w i

decls.name: TauCeti.finite_end_of_smulCommClass
decls.doc:
Finiteness over a base ring `K` whose action on `M` commutes with the `R`-action gives the
finiteness hypothesis density needs: the `K`-scalars are themselves `R`-linear endomorphisms of `M`,
so `M` is finite over `Module.End R M` along the tower `K → Module.End R M → M`.
decls.statement:
theorem finite_end_of_smulCommClass (K : Type*) [Semiring K] [Module K M] [SMulCommClass R K M]
    [Module.Finite K M] : Module.Finite (Module.End R M) M

decls.name: TauCeti.algEquivEndEndOfIsSimpleRing
decls.doc:
**The double centralizer theorem for a finite module over a simple algebra.** If `R` is a
simple `K`-algebra and `M` a simple `R`-module which is finite as a `K`-module, then `M` presents
`R` as the algebra of `D`-linear endomorphisms of `M`, where `D = Module.End R M`. This is the form
in which Layer 3 of the roadmap is consumed by the central-simple theory.
decls.title: The double centralizer theorem for a finite module over a simple algebra
decls.statement:
def algEquivEndEndOfIsSimpleRing (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] [Algebra K R]
    [Module K M] [IsScalarTower K R M] [Module.Finite K M] [IsSimpleRing R] [IsSimpleModule R M] :
    R ≃ₐ[K] Module.End (Module.End R M) M

decls.name: TauCeti.algEquivEndEndOfIsSimpleRing_apply
decls.statement:
theorem algEquivEndEndOfIsSimpleRing_apply (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] [Algebra K R] [Module K M]
    [IsScalarTower K R M] [Module.Finite K M] [IsSimpleRing R] [IsSimpleModule R M] (r : R)
    (m : M) :
    algEquivEndEndOfIsSimpleRing R M K r m = r • m

decls.name: TauCeti.algEquivEndEndOfIsSimpleRing_symm_smul
decls.statement:
theorem algEquivEndEndOfIsSimpleRing_symm_smul (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] [Algebra K R]
    [Module K M] [IsScalarTower K R M] [Module.Finite K M] [IsSimpleRing R] [IsSimpleModule R M]
    (f : Module.End (Module.End R M) M) (m : M) :
    (algEquivEndEndOfIsSimpleRing R M K).symm f • m = f m
